name: SoFi Stadium
public_transport: Metro C Line to Inglewood/Downtown Landing station
notes: Largest World Cup venue. Book hotels 3+ months early — LA has limited affordable stock near the stadium.

name: MetLife Stadium
public_transport: NJ Transit train to Meadowlands Sports Complex station on match days only
fan_zone: Times Square Fan Festival and MetLife plaza
notes: Final venue. Stay in NYC and take NJ Transit — much better options than East Rutherford hotels.

name: AT&T Stadium
public_transport: Trinity Railway Express to CentrePort/DFW, then shuttle on match days
fan_zone: AT&T Plaza and Six Flags area
notes: Texas heat in June/July — expect 38–42°C. Stay hydrated. The stadium is fully air-conditioned indoors.

name: Rose Bowl Stadium
public_transport: Metro Gold Line to Memorial Park station, then shuttle
fan_zone: Rose Bowl parking lots and Pasadena Old Town
notes: Second largest World Cup venue. Old Town Pasadena is the best pre-match area — excellent food and atmosphere within walking distance of the Metro.

name: BC Place
public_transport: Canada Line SkyTrain to Stadium-Chinatown station — 5 min walk
fan_zone: David Lam Park and Robson Square
notes: Best-connected World Cup venue — SkyTrain runs directly from airport to the stadium. Downtown Vancouver hotels are excellent value vs US cities.

name: Estadio Azteca
public_transport: Metro Line 2 to Tasqueña, then tram to Estadio Azteca
fan_zone: Foro Sol adjacent complex and Zócalo Plaza
notes: At 2,240m altitude — expect breathlessness for a day or two. Most affordable host city. Polanco neighbourhood is the safest and most tourist-friendly base.

name: Estadio Akron
public_transport: BRT Macrobús Line 1 to Estadio Akron
fan_zone: Andares Shopping Centre and Estadio plaza
notes: Guadalajara is the tequila capital of Mexico — explore the centro histórico before or after matches. Very affordable compared to US venues.

name: Lumen Field
public_transport: Link Light Rail from Sea-Tac airport to Stadium station — direct
fan_zone: Occidental Square and CenturyLink Field plaza
notes: June weather in Seattle is mild and often overcast — bring a light jacket. Pioneer Square neighbourhood is ideal for pre-match food and bars.

name: Soldier Field
public_transport: CTA Red Line to Roosevelt, then bus 146 or 20 min walk along the lakefront
fan_zone: Grant Park and Museum Campus lakefront
notes: Beautiful lakefront setting — arrive early to walk the Museum Campus. The Loop has excellent hotel options at reasonable prices for a major US city.

name: Hard Rock Stadium
public_transport: Tri-Rail to Miami Airport, then shuttle on match days
fan_zone: South Beach Fan Festival and stadium parking
notes: Intense heat and humidity in June/July — 32–36°C with high humidity. Stay on South Beach for the full Miami experience; plan 45–60 min travel to stadium.

name: Arrowhead Stadium
public_transport: Match day shuttles from Union Station and Crown Center
fan_zone: Power & Light District and Crown Center
notes: Most affordable US host city. Famous for BBQ — visit Joe's Kansas City or Q39 before the match. Power & Light District is lively on match nights.

name: Gillette Stadium
public_transport: Commuter Rail from South Station Boston to Foxboro on match days
fan_zone: Patriot Place adjacent retail and dining complex
notes: Stay in Boston and take the match day commuter rail — far better hotels and atmosphere. Patriot Place has good pre-match dining options right at the stadium.
